## My Thinking

I have been working this land for 40 years. I know this soil, I know Quzhou's weather, and I know what my family needs. My wheat-maize rotation is the backbone of everything — it goes on the best 4 mu. It is reliable, I can sell the grain or store it, and after harvest I just direct-seed the maize straight into the wheat stubble. That saves my back and saves fuel.

Cotton I keep on 2 mu. It is exhausting work — lots of spraying, picking is hard, and the price is never quite what you hope — but it is cash. My daughter-in-law helps during picking. If I had worse joints I might cut it, but not yet.

The last 1 mu goes to watermelon in spring. The neighbors and the road-side traders come to me. It is not worth scaling up because watermelon takes a lot of attention and water, and I only have one well.

For fertilizer I apply what I know works here. I am not going to experiment with cutting nitrogen — I tried that once about fifteen years ago and lost yield. I use a little more potassium on the watermelon and cotton because those crops pull it out of the ground hard.

I irrigate wheat three times — before sowing, over winter, and at jointing. Maize I usually only need twice unless July is very dry. Cotton and watermelon both need more water because they are out there all summer in the heat.

For tillage: rotary on the wheat ground after maize harvest in October, no-till direct seeding for the summer maize after wheat, and I plough the cotton and watermelon plots in spring.
